stories.headline: Fed sees AI boom adding to inflation pressure
stories.summary: Federal Reserve officials increasingly view AI investment as an inflationary demand shock. Because large AI firms are less sensitive to interest rates, economists warn that efforts to cool inflation may fall disproportionately on households and smaller businesses.

stories.headline: Control of Congress at stake in US midterms
stories.summary: Early voting is underway before November 3. Republicans hold narrow House and Senate majorities; Democrats need four net seats in each chamber. Ten Senate contests could decide control, while polling and turnout remain uncertain.

stories.headline: China growth rebounds but consumers remain weak
stories.summary: China's third-quarter growth accelerated to 4.5%, beating expectations as exports surged. Retail sales lagged industrial output and property remained weak, leaving the recovery dependent on foreign demand and vulnerable to trade restrictions.

stories.headline: Russian strike hits Kyiv subway and homes
stories.summary: Kyiv's mayor said a Russian strike killed one woman, injured three people and damaged a subway station, residential building and medical facility. Zelenskiy said the US has resumed intelligence sharing needed for missile warnings.

stories.headline: WFP cuts food aid for 500,000 people in Gaza
stories.summary: The World Food Programme says funding shortages are cutting monthly assistance from 1.6 million to 1.1 million recipients. Rations, cash support and hot meals are also being reduced while about 1.4 million people face crisis-level food insecurity.
